dashed-keywords.comment: `keiro-dsl` is the dialect name in the `language keiro-dsl 1` version preamble. It is the one entry here whose leading segment is not itself a keyword, so it needs no ordering care beyond being in this rule at all — without it the spelling falls through as plain text.
dashed-keywords.name: keyword.control.keiro

mapped-decl-with-name.comment: The family or shape word of a `mapped` declaration plus the type name it names. Listed before #modifiers so it wins the same-position tie and can claim both tokens; its first capture keeps the Modifier scope those four words carry on their own. `nominal` is the third family (`mapped nominal X : Text { ... }`), added by keiro-dsl fcd6748.

introducers.comment: `language` opens the optional version preamble (`language keiro-dsl 1`), the only clause above `context`. Matched unconditionally: the parser's first-significant-line placement rule is not something a lexical grammar models.
introducers.name: keyword.declaration.keiro

modifiers.comment: `nominal` joins `structural` and `opaque` as a `mapped` family word: `pMappedTopItem` upstream reads `keyword "mapped"` and then chooses between the three, so all three qualify the declaration `mapped` introduces rather than introducing one.
modifiers.name: storage.modifier.keiro

types.comment: `Map` (capitalized) is a primitive type; the reserved lowercase `map` is a control keyword. Oniguruma is case-sensitive, and #types is listed before #control-keywords. `Integer` (keiro-dsl 8b0f55b) is a distinct spelling from `Int`, not an alias — upstream uses `Int` for machine integers and `Integer` for exact arbitrary-precision ones. It is listed before `Int` for readability only: the trailing `(?![A-Za-z0-9_])` already stops `Int` from claiming the head of `Integer`.
types.name: support.type.keiro

scalar-roots.comment: The two roots of a version-2 scalar expression: `reg.balance` reads a register, `cmd.balance` reads a field of the command being handled. Same class as the older dotted roots `input.` and `timer.`, but matched ONLY when a `.` follows. Upstream's `pScalarPath` gives these words meaning only as the head of a dotted path, and `cmd` is already a wire word in five corpus files (`id CommandId prefix=cmd`) that an unconditional rule would recolour. See Section 4 of spec/keiro-dsl-language-model.md.
scalar-roots.name: keyword.control.keiro

control-keywords.comment: `using` introduces the consumer binding block on an `id` or `enum` declaration (`id OrderId prefix=ord using { ... }`). It opens a clause of a declaration another word already began — like `wire` inside a `mapped structural` block — so it belongs here rather than with the modifiers. `implementation` opens the transition clause `implementation hole` (keiro-dsl 8b0f55b), a peer of `guard`, `write`, `emit`, and `goto`; its second word `hole` is in #constants and stays there.
control-keywords.name: keyword.control.keiro

numbers.comment: Longest form first: TextMate takes the first listed alternative that matches at a position, so `\b[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\b` must precede `\b[0-9]+\b` or `1.5` tokenizes as `1` `.` `5`. This is the opposite of the order packages/keiro-vim/syntax/keiro.vim needs, where Vim's tie-break favours the item defined last — do not sync the two orderings.

operators.comment: `*` multiplies two operands of a version-2 scalar expression (`write x := reg.x * 2`). The matching subtraction operator is a bare `-`, deliberately absent: Section 5 of spec/keiro-dsl-language-model.md lists `-->`, `--`, and `->` but no bare `-`, and a rule for one would colour the dash inside every wire word.
operators.name: keyword.operator.keiro
